neighbours.label: a publication or organization name as the subject about to call / name / deem something (Time magazine, the Washington Post)
fire: In 2004, Time magazine named her one of the most influential people in the world.
Last spring the Washington Post called the plan a bold gamble.
The World Health Organization deemed the clinic a model of good practice.
In 1999, Rolling Stone magazine ranked the album among the best of the decade.
Forbes magazine listed him among the richest men in Asia.
The New York Times described the novel as a quiet masterpiece.
Wired magazine hailed the device as the gadget of the year.
The United Nations declared the region a disaster zone.
quiet: In 2004, my neighbor gave her one of the old chairs from the attic.
Last spring the city council approved the plan after a long debate.
The local doctor treated the patients at the clinic every Tuesday.
In 1999, my brother bought the album at a shop downtown.
My uncle met him at a conference in Asia.
My teacher lent me the novel over the summer.
My cousin dropped the device on the kitchen floor.
The farmers left the region after the flood.

notes: Logit effect: the - pole promotes ' called', ' named', ' labeled', ' termed'.
